Motivation

This PR introduces Ring Attention to enable memory-efficient and scalable attention for long-sequence transformers. By streaming attention computations in a ring-like pattern, it reduces GPU memory usage and computation overhead while preserving numerical stability. The implementation integrates with existing FlashAttention kernels, supports KV caching, and causal masking. This enhancement improves performance for long-context models.

Code Review

This pull request introduces a RingAttentionBackend and an AttnContextParallelCommunicate class to support ring-based context parallel attention. Several critical issues were identified: the asynchronous communication logic in send_recv_kvcache returns unpopulated tensors before the operations complete, leading to incorrect attention results in the backend. Additionally, the communicator is inefficiently instantiated on every forward pass, and there are multiple references to an undefined self.rank attribute in logging statements across the communication module.

There was a problem hiding this comment.

Choose a reason for hiding this comment

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more.

The send_recv_kvcache method returns result_tensor immediately after initiating asynchronous isend and irecv operations. At this point, result_tensor is still filled with zeros from torch.zeros_like and has not received the actual data from the peer. The commit and wait methods are designed for deferred execution, meaning the data will only be available after wait() is called. Returning result_tensor here makes it unusable for the caller to get the actual received data. This is a critical logic error that will lead to incorrect computations.

The cp_ring_comm.send_recv(k) and cp_ring_comm.send_recv(v) calls will return uninitialized tensors (filled with zeros) because of a critical bug in the AttnContextParallelCommunicate.send_recv_kvcache method. This means next_k and next_v will not contain the actual data from the previous rank in the ring. Consequently, the flash_attn_with_kvcache call will use incorrect (zeroed-out) key and value tensors for subsequent steps, leading to completely wrong attention computations. This is a critical bug that needs immediate attention.

Choose a reason for hiding this comment

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more.

Instantiating AttnContextParallelCommunicate() inside the forward_extend method means a new communicator object is created for every forward pass. This is inefficient and can lead to unnecessary overhead or resource contention in a distributed environment. Communicator objects should ideally be initialized once and reused across multiple calls to forward_extend.

Consider initializing AttnContextParallelCommunicate as a member of RingAttentionBackend in its __init__ method, or passing an already initialized instance.
